scope: Ten EU/EEA industrial and energy candidates; historical confirmed named support relationships, with indirect exposure isolated
date_policy: Use captured dated public confirmation. When the exact award day is unknown, event_date is conservatively the confirmation day and limitations disclose that choice. Completed funding periods do not erase historical recipient status. end_date is an ownership/eligibility endpoint, not a project-completion date.

events.programme: UK aerospace R&D and skills grants disclosed to Parliament
events.beneficiary: EADS and its subsidiaries, including Airbus

sources.title: House of Commons written answer: EADS public funding
sources.evidence: The minister confirmed that EADS received UK grants for R&D and skills activities in FY2012/13, separately mentioning defence procurement and repayable loans.

events.rationale: Ancillary confirmation of grants to the Airbus predecessor; excluded from main admission because neither an individual programme nor project is identified.
events.limitations: The parliamentary answer aggregates R&D and skills grants, loans and procurement without naming the grant programme. The separate 2014 ATI project supplies the main qualifying evidence.
events.award_amount_note: Company-specific award amount is not established in the recorded evidence. Null is unknown, not zero.

events.programme: Aerospace Technology Institute: Broughton wing manufacturing R&D

sources.title: Prime Minister hails 1,800 jobs in Britain at UK Investment Summit
sources.evidence: UK and Welsh governments announced investment with Airbus, including approximately GBP64m of R&D activity through ATI and a GBP48m Broughton wing-manufacturing project.

events.rationale: Named government-supported industrial R&D projects at an Airbus subsidiary, providing a specifically identified programme in addition to the 2013 receipt confirmation.
events.limitations: Figures are total joint investment/project budgets, not government grants paid solely to Airbus; no unsupported grant amount is assigned.
events.award_amount_note: Broughton project budget, not the public contribution or Airbus-only award.

events.programme: FP7 Clean Sky: Open Rotor / Sustainable and Green Engines
events.beneficiary: Safran and its Open Rotor industrial research consortium

sources.title: Safran celebrates successful start of Open Rotor demonstrator tests
sources.evidence: Safran confirmed that it and its partners had received EUR65m of European Commission funding for the Open Rotor project over eight years.

events.rationale: An explicitly funded industrial R&D programme, with both Safran's role and past EU funding confirmed in a dated issuer release.
events.limitations: The project began in 2008 but this publication is not backdated to that year. EUR65m is a consortium total. Earlier annual reports establish participation in VITAL, DREAM and Clean Sky but the captured passages do not separately establish a dated grant award or receipt.
events.award_amount_note: Total European Commission funding to Safran and its partners; Safran share unknown.

sources.title: GRID4EU Increasing Power for Renewables
sources.evidence: Enel identifies Enel Distribuzione as a GRID4EU partner with an Italian distribution-grid demonstration; the EUR54m programme includes EUR25m of EU funding.

events.rationale: Named controlled operating company participates in a funded industrial smart-grid demonstration, rather than merely selling into a generally subsidised sector.
events.limitations: The programme launched in 2011; the admission date uses this dated confirmation, not its earlier project start. The EU contribution is programme-wide, not Enel's individual grant.
events.award_amount_note: EU contribution within EUR54m programme; Enel share unknown.

events.programme: UK FID Enabling for Renewables: Burbo Bank Extension, Walney Extension and Hornsea 1

sources.evidence: The decision dated 23 July 2014 raises no objections to the five named offshore-wind aid measures. Paragraph 45 records that contracts were signed in May subject to Commission approval. The approval notice appeared in OJ C393 on 7 November 2014.

sources.title: Government unveils eight major new renewables projects
sources.evidence: DECC awarded early CfD investment contracts and named DONG Energy Wind Power A/S as developer of Burbo Bank Extension, Hornsea 1 and Walney Extension.

sources.title: FID Enabling for Renewables: Investment Contracts
sources.evidence: DECC subsequently published the signed investment contracts, laid before Parliament on 4 June 2014.

sources.title: Official Journal C116: Lynemouth state-aid proceeding, footnote 2
sources.evidence: The official publication identifies the earlier five-wind-farm no-objection decision of 23 July 2014 and its OJ C393/2014 publication. This is bibliographic corroboration only, not an earlier information date.

events.limitations: The decision was adopted on 23 July 2014; original approval-day press content was not readable in this capture, so the documented 7 November 2014 Official Journal publication is used conservatively. Conditional April award and June publication of signed contracts alone do not trigger admission. IPO tradability starts in June 2016.
events.award_amount_note: Company-specific award amount is not established in the recorded evidence. Null is unknown, not zero.

events.rationale: Vestas is a named participant in the government-funded industrial development project.
events.limitations: DKK47m is shared project funding, not an asserted Vestas-only receipt. Earlier wind-research partnerships were located but original public grant dates and Vestas's continuing participation were not resolved. No exact completion day is inferred from the three-year duration.

events.beneficiary: Siemens Gas and Power business inherited by Siemens Energy

sources.title: HYFLEXPOWER: The world's first integrated power-to-X-to-power hydrogen gas turbine demonstrator
sources.evidence: Siemens Gas and Power is a named HYFLEXPOWER partner; Horizon 2020 funds EUR10.5m of the EUR15.2m demonstrator. The release identifies the energy business planned to operate as Siemens Energy.

sources.title: Siemens Energy's debut on the stock market
sources.evidence: The issuer confirmed first trading on 28 September 2020 following the successful spin-off of Siemens Gas and Power.

events.rationale: The documented funded business was inherited by Siemens Energy, and admission is conservatively dated to public confirmation of the completed separation and listing.
events.limitations: The project began in May 2020. No Siemens AG investment history or share-price history is treated as Siemens Energy's pre-spin-off history. The EU funding is a consortium total; the four-year project horizon does not terminate historical recipient eligibility.
events.award_amount_note: EU funding within EUR15.2m demonstrator; Siemens Energy share unknown.

events.programme: Akershus County Council hydrogen station public-private partnership

sources.title: Public-private partnership agreement with Akershus County Council
sources.evidence: Nel's hydrogen subsidiary entered a county agreement for a hydrogen station; the signed agreement provides for a county grant toward completion.

sources.title: Cavendish Hydrogen lists on Euronext Oslo Børs
sources.evidence: The exchange announced the completed separation and listing of Nel's fueling division as Cavendish Hydrogen.

events.rationale: A named, signed government grant relationship at a controlled subsidiary, rather than an unawarded programme or ordinary procurement.
events.limitations: The release says the grant will be awarded under the agreement; it does not confirm payment or amount. The funded business is conservatively no longer attributed to Nel after the 2024 fueling separation; a separate 2016 retained-business R&D event independently supports subsequent eligibility. The exact allocation of this older station agreement between retained and separated entities is not established; the conservative cutoff avoids relying on it after separation.
events.ownership_end_basis: Conservative research cutoff at the public completed fueling separation; whether this particular older agreement was transferred is unresolved. The retained electrolyser HYPER programme separately qualifies.
events.award_amount_note: Company-specific award amount is not established in the recorded evidence. Null is unknown, not zero.

sources.title: NEL to receive grant from Enova SF
sources.evidence: Nel identified NEL Fuel Norway AS as its subsidiary and announced an Enova grant exceeding NOK7.5m for an Oslo-area hydrogen station.

sources.title: NEL enters into final agreement with Uno-X for hydrogen station network
sources.evidence: Nel announced the final joint venture agreement under which Uno-X Hydrogen is owned 51% by Uno-X and 49% by Nel.

events.rationale: Explicit targeted grant award to the then-described subsidiary.
events.limitations: The station-network vehicle subsequently became a minority joint venture. This event is conservatively ended when the final 49% agreement was publicly announced, without claiming continued controlled-subsidiary status.
events.award_amount_note: Release says grant exceeds NOK7.5m; this is a lower bound, not an exact amount.

events.programme: Research Council of Norway ENERGIX: HYPER hydrogen production study
events.beneficiary: NEL ASA, industrial partner in SINTEF-led HYPER

sources.title: NEL initiates feasibility partner study for large-scale hydrogen production in Norway
sources.evidence: Nel announced its participation in HYPER and confirmed that the project received a NOK14m ENERGIX grant toward a NOK20m research programme financed through 2019.

events.rationale: Named industrial participation in funded hydrogen-production R&D, linked to Nel's retained electrolyser activity rather than only its later-separated fueling business.
events.limitations: The grant is to the consortium, hosted by SINTEF; no individual Nel cash amount is claimed. The source gives only a financing horizon through 2019, so no exact completion date or eligibility expiry is invented.
events.award_amount_note: ENERGIX grant within NOK20m project; Nel share unknown.
